Shows both floor-test outcomes and the exceptional supported-floor call.

facts.rationale: The previous explanation covered floor maintenance and floor loss but omitted the common helper's exceptional supported-floor branch. This correction preserves that branch without assigning an unverified meaning to its predicate or callee.
facts.value: While Harisen state 0 is active, this callback delegates to it_8026D62C with it_8029290C and then returns false. The helper refreshes collision-derived position and records the supporting-floor index when its floor test succeeds. If the floor test fails, it performs leave-ground setup and invokes it_8029290C, selecting falling state 1. On the supported-floor path, it can instead call Item_8026ADC0 when it_80277544(gobj) is nonzero and Item.xDCD_flag.b3 is clear; floor support therefore does not unconditionally guarantee that the item remains in state 0.

facts.rationale: The previous explanation incorrectly restricted fighter-side uses to command 2. The canonical take-damage callback also invokes this helper under a non-null held-item guard, establishing an interruption path in addition to the scripted swing transition.
facts.value: Restores the Harisen item's animation speed to 1.0 and enters motion state 6 with ITEM_ANIM_UPDATE. Fighter-side Harisen processing uses this transition both when consuming swing command 2 and when the wielding fighter takes damage; the damage path first restores the held item's common scale.
